subject: science
title: 3D Molecule Builder — Atoms, Molecular Mass & Percent Composition
subtitle: Modern atomic theory, Relative Atomic Mass (C-12 scale), atomicity, and gram molecular mass
curiosity_hook: How do chemists weigh invisible molecules like water (H₂O) or carbon dioxide (CO₂) using Carbon-12 as a balance standard?
source_verified_by: AGY Pass 2 3D Blueprint Build (pending human chemistry teacher sign-off)
learning_objectives: Inspect 3D molecular models (H₂O, CO₂, CH₄) to determine atomicity and classify homoatomic vs heteroatomic molecules.
Compute Relative Molecular Mass and Gram Molecular Mass from Table 7.1 C-12 Relative Atomic Masses (H=1, C=12, N=14, O=16).
Calculate percent composition by mass of each element in a compound and explain why atomic masses in the periodic table are weighted isotopic averages.

concept_outline.heading: Relative Atomic Mass & Average Atomic Mass (7.1–7.1.2)
concept_outline.summary: Unified atomic mass unit (u) equals 1/12th the mass of one Carbon-12 atom. Naturally occurring elements are mixtures of isotopes, so periodic-table atomic masses are weighted averages (e.g., Carbon = 12×0.989 + 13×0.011 = 12.011 amu).

concept_outline.heading: Atomicity & Classification of Molecules (7.2–7.2.1)
concept_outline.summary: Atomicity is the total number of atoms in one molecule. Homoatomic molecules contain identical elements (O₂, O₃, P₄); heteroatomic molecules contain different elements (H₂O, CO₂, CH₄).

concept_outline.heading: Gram Molecular Mass & Percent Composition (7.5)
concept_outline.summary: Summing relative atomic masses of all constituent atoms yields Relative Molecular Mass (expressed in grams = Gram Molecular Mass). Percent composition = (Mass of element in 1 mole / Molar mass) × 100.

key_terms.definition: Total number of atoms constituting one molecule (e.g. H₂O has atomicity 3; CH₄ has atomicity 5).
Ratio of average mass of isotopes of an element to 1/12th the mass of one Carbon-12 atom (dimensionless).
A molecule made of atoms of two or more different elements, such as H₂O or CO₂.
Percentage by mass of each element present in a pure chemical compound.

controls.label: 3D Molecule Selector
controls.description: Switch between H₂O, CO₂, CH₄, and organic molecules in 3D ball-and-stick mode.

controls.label: Click-to-Inspect Atoms
controls.description: Click any 3D or 2D atom sphere to read its element symbol, Table 7.1 Ar value, and structural role.
controls.keyboard_equivalent: Inspect full element mass breakdown table alongside the 2D structural projection.

expected_observations: Water (H₂O) has bent geometry (104.5°), atomicity 3, molecular mass 18 g/mol, and 88.89% Oxygen by mass.
Carbon dioxide (CO₂) is linear (180°) with two double bonds, atomicity 3, and molecular mass 44 g/mol.
limitations: Ball-and-stick 3D models visualize covalent bond geometry and atom counts clearly; atomic radii are scaled schematically.

storyboard.title: Inspect Water (H₂O) in 3D
storyboard.learner_action: Orbit H₂O and click the central red Oxygen atom.
storyboard.expected_response: Atom readout shows Oxygen (Ar = 16); total Gram Molecular Mass = 18 g/mol.

storyboard.title: Compare Linear CO₂ Double Bonds
storyboard.expected_response: Two parallel cylinders on each side of Carbon show O=C=O linear double bonding (44 g/mol).

storyboard.title: Verify Percent Composition
storyboard.learner_action: Compare % Carbon in CO₂ (27.27%) vs CH₄ (75.00%).
storyboard.expected_response: Hydrogen is much lighter (Ar = 1) than Oxygen (Ar = 16), so Carbon dominates CH₄ by mass.

accessible_equivalent.summary: 2D interactive structural SVG projection and complete Table 7.1 atomic-mass & percent-composition breakdown without WebGL.

steps.heading: Count Every Atom (Atomicity)
steps.description: Read subscripts in the formula: H₂O has 2 H + 1 O = 3 atoms (triatomic).
steps.key_takeaway: Atomicity = total number of atoms in one molecule.

steps.heading: Multiply by Table 7.1 Atomic Mass
steps.description: Use H = 1, C = 12, N = 14, O = 16 to sum total molecular mass.

steps.heading: Compute Percent by Mass
steps.description: Divide each element's mass contribution by total molecular mass and multiply by 100.
steps.key_takeaway: All element percentages always sum to 100%.

question_bank.prompt: Which isotope is used as the modern international standard for Relative Atomic Mass (Ar)?

options.label: Hydrogen-1
options.feedback: Hydrogen was an early historical standard later replaced.

options.label: Carbon-12
options.feedback: Correct! 1 amu (u) is defined as 1/12th the mass of one stable Carbon-12 atom.

options.label: Oxygen-18
options.feedback: Oxygen was used historically before Carbon-12 became the unified standard.

options.label: Nitrogen-14
options.feedback: Nitrogen-14 is not the reference standard.

question_bank.worked_explanation: Modern mass spectrometry and IUPAC define 1 u as 1/12th the mass of a Carbon-12 atom.

question_bank.prompt: Using Table 7.1 (H = 1, O = 16), what is the Gram Molecular Mass of Water (H₂O) and its atomicity?

options.label: 17 g/mol, atomicity 2
options.feedback: Water has TWO hydrogen atoms, not one.

options.label: 18 g/mol, atomicity 3
options.feedback: Correct! 2(1) + 16 = 18 g/mol, and 2 H + 1 O = 3 atoms (heteroatomic triatomic).

options.label: 18 g/mol, atomicity 2
options.feedback: Water contains 2 different elements but 3 total atoms, so atomicity is 3.

question_bank.worked_explanation: H₂O contains 2 H atoms and 1 O atom → atomicity = 3; Gram Molecular Mass = 2(1) + 16 = 18 g.

question_bank.prompt: Boron occurs naturally as 20% Boron-10 and 80% Boron-11 (Textbook p. 94). What is its Average Atomic Mass?

options.label: 10.2 amu
options.feedback: Check which isotope has the 80% abundance (Boron-11).

options.label: 11.0 amu
options.feedback: The 20% Boron-10 pulls the weighted average down to 10.8 amu.

worked_feedback: Distinguish carefully between number of elements (2 in H₂O) and atomicity (total atoms = 3 in H₂O).
Check that fractional isotopic abundances sum to 1.00 (100%).

flashcards.back: Exactly 1/12th the mass of one Carbon-12 isotope atom.
Homoatomic has identical atoms (O₂, O₃); Heteroatomic has different elements (H₂O, CO₂, CH₄).

flashcards.front: Percent of Carbon in CO₂ (C=12, O=16)
